key_insight: Pretrained large-scale video generation models implicitly encode rich 3D spatial priors that can be extracted and repurposed to give multimodal systems fine-grained geometric and physical reasoning without explicit 3D supervision.
problem_solved: Multimodal models are spatially blind — they struggle with depth, occlusion, object relationships and physical dynamics — and current fixes rely on scarce explicit 3D data or complex geometric scaffolding that hurt generalization.
method: Probe and extract implicit spatial/3D priors from pretrained video generation model latents or intermediate representations.
Integrate these priors into scene-understanding pipelines via lightweight adapters or conditioning to improve depth, occlusion, and dynamics predictions.
Fine-tune or align with small supervisory signals (synthetic cues, multi-view consistency) to transfer priors to downstream tasks while avoiding large 3D datasets.
impact: Provides a practical way to boost spatial reasoning in multimodal systems using existing video models, reducing dependence on costly 3D data. This enables better generalization for tasks like robotics, AR, and physical-scene QA with minimal extra annotation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained video generator -> latent probing/extraction -> adapter/conditioning -> downstream scene tasks (depth, occlusion, dynamics).
Before/after qualitative panels: example images with model outputs (depth maps, occlusion masks, predicted trajectories) showing improvements.
Performance chart: relative metrics (accuracy/IoU/error) comparing baseline multimodal model vs. model augmented with video-derived 3D priors across several tasks.
Icon set: camera/video reel (source), brain/latent (implicit priors), wrench/adapter (integration), dart/target (downstream tasks) to visually summarize the approach.
paper_title: Generation Models Know Space: Unleashing Implicit 3D Priors for Scene Understanding
paper_authors: Xianjin Wu, Dingkang Liang, Tianrui Feng, Kui Xia, Yumeng Zhang
